title: Ensure backend runtime parameters are configured correctly
rationale: Backend runtime parameters influence PostgreSQL performance, stability, and security. They should be reviewed to ensure they meet organizational requirements.
remediation: Review backend runtime parameters such as work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, shared_buffers, effective_cache_size, and other runtime settings according to workload requirements.

title: Ensure Postmaster runtime parameters are configured
rationale: Postmaster parameters affect server startup and overall database behavior. They should be configured according to security and operational requirements.
remediation: Review startup parameters including max_connections, superuser_reserved_connections, shared_preload_libraries, and related postmaster settings.

title: Ensure SIGHUP runtime parameters are configured
rationale: SIGHUP parameters can be reloaded without restarting PostgreSQL and should be reviewed to maintain secure and reliable operation.
remediation: Review reloadable configuration parameters and ensure they align with organizational standards.

title: Ensure Superuser runtime parameters are configured
rationale: Runtime parameters that require superuser privileges should be reviewed carefully to prevent insecure or unsupported configurations.
remediation: Review all superuser-controlled runtime parameters and ensure they comply with organizational security policies.

title: Ensure User runtime parameters are configured
rationale: User-configurable runtime parameters should be reviewed to ensure they do not weaken security or impact database performance.
remediation: Review role- and session-level runtime parameters assigned through ALTER ROLE and ALTER DATABASE statements.
